title: Late-shift mini braintrust — quick triage + micro-experiments
content:
Context / why this exists:
- Late shift run: quick brain-dump after handoff time. Keep short, actionable.
- Focus: two noisy p99 regressions + a flakey KV cache eviction pattern observed on rwinf-3147.

Quick summary (1-2 lines):
- p99 token generation increased ~12% in worker-3 on short sequences (<=64) since kernel push 2026-03-10. Suspect scheduling bump + small-batch path.
- Pattern: KV cache evictions spike when autoscaler scales down GPU pods and a small-batch burst returns mid-scale-up.

Immediate triage checklist (do first):
- [ ] Reproduce short-seq p99 locally with workload sim: use tests/perf/sim_short_seq --concurrency 8 --seed 42.
- [ ] Enable trace-level logs on worker-3 (temp): export RWINF_LOG=trace && restart runtime-service on node e5.
- [ ] Add eviction counter to metrics pipeline (prometheus label: eviction_on_scale) and shim a quick dashboard alert.

Observations / raw traces (notes to self):
- trace_20260312T23:11: two KV evictions within 3s around scale-down event. Eviction policy: lru-ttl 120s. But workload shows many ephemeral prefixes => thrash.
- sampling: small batch fraction increased from 18% -> 31% after kernel patch that changed batching threshold from 6->4 tokens. Might be inverse effect.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching threshold tweak forced more very-small batches, pushing runtime into an under-optimized path that has a heavier context-setup cost. (high confidence)
2) Autoscaler scale-down race clears prefetched KV shards; scale-up returns with warmup penalty causing p99 spikes. (med confidence)
3) New kernel memory allocator path has slightly different NUMA placement for small allocations — increases latency variance. (low confidence)

Small experiments to run (safe, low-risk):
- EXP-A: revert batching threshold from 4 -> 6 in a canary pool (dev1) and replay trace for 2h. Metric: p99 tokens and small-batch ratio. (command: ./deploy/canary.sh --patch batching.threshold=6 --pool dev1)
- EXP-B: increase KV TTL window to 300s on a single node to measure eviction rate changes (prometheus:kv_evictions_total). (k8s patch applied to node label test-ttl)
- EXP-C: force affinity pinning off (fallback allocator) for one pod to compare allocator path latencies.

Notes for commands / snippets to run quickly:
- repro agent: python infra/perf/repro.py --scenario short_seq --workers 8 --cpu 4 --gpus 0.5
- quick prometheus query: rate(kv_evictions_total{job="runtime"}[5m])
- dump recent traces: ./tools/trace_fetcher --from 2026-03-12T22:50 --to 2026-03-12T23:20 --node worker-3 > /tmp/trace-w3.json

Things to push to ticket RWINF-3147 (what I'll add tomorrow):
- attach mini repro (EXP-A logs) + raw trace snippet showing two evictions in 3s.
- propose rollout: canary revert of batching threshold + monitor for 48h.

Open questions / unresolved:
- If we raise TTL, does memory pressure cause larger GC events that hurt throughput? Need mem pressure test.
- Are there other places changing batching threshold besides the kernel patch? Search PR history for keyword "threshold" in serving-runtime repo.

Hand-off notes (to oncoming shift):
- If page: start with EXP-A repro (it's quickest).
- If p99 keeps rising: disable small-batch path via feature-flag small_batch_opt=false and scale up canary.
- Escalation: ping @ravi and @ivy in slack channel #runtime-ops and paste the /tmp/trace-w3.json snippet.

Personal TODO (short):
- [ ] run EXP-A tonight (30m)
- [ ] add eviction-on-scale tag to prometheus metrics (15m)
- [ ] open minimal PR for canary revert with test plan (45m)

Micro-random thoughts (sleepy brain):
- Maybe we should add a "burst window" metric to the router that tracks recent small-batch ratio at 10s granularity. Could be a cheap signal for routing away from small-batch optimized pools.
- Worth a short blurb in tomorrow standup: "Observed p99 bump linked to batching threshold change — running canary revert." Keep it short.

Ending note: keep this file as a quick scratch. Save outputs into /home/leila/tmp/late-shift/ and push artifacts to RWINF-3147. If I forget, check linked artifacts above for the github PR and slack thread.

-- Leila
